acceptedSevenLeaves.oldValue: Holy water circle, or burning incense; reverse uses blood or smoldering dung
acceptedSevenLeaves.newValue: 3′-diameter circle on floor or ground: holy water for protection from evil, blood for protection from good; alternatively, in the air using burning incense or smoldering dung with respect to evil/good.
acceptedSevenLeaves.finding: Ground/floor materials are separated for Protection from Evil and Protection from Good; the alternate in-air material pair follows the source evil/good order. The proposed phrase is accepted; adding “respectively” would be optional editorial clarification only.

acceptedSevenLeaves.oldValue: A 1-foot barrier prevents bodily contact by the enchanted, conjured and summoned creatures described in the source.
acceptedSevenLeaves.newValue: A ward one foot from the recipient prevents bodily contact by enchanted or conjured beings, including aerial servants, demons, devils, djinn, efreet, elementals, imps, invisible stalkers, night hags, quasits, salamanders, water weirds, wind walkers and xorn; summoned animals or monsters are similarly kept away.
acceptedSevenLeaves.finding: The one-foot ward, full enchanted/conjured list, and separate summoned animals/monsters result are accurately represented.

acceptedSevenLeaves.oldValue: Retrieval normally gains 4 free surprise rounds; a target able to detect invisibility uses the source’s surprise roll. A successful hit grabs the target, followed by a strength comparison.
acceptedSevenLeaves.newValue: When sent on a mission, the servant attacks by complete surprise and gains 4 free melee rounds unless the creature involved can detect invisible objects; then roll 1d6: 1 = 1 free round, 2 = 2, 3 = 3, 4 = 4, and 5 or 6 = 0 (the opponent is not surprised). Each round, the servant rolls to hit; a hit means it grabbed the assigned object or creature. If a creature is involved, compare strength; if it has no strength rating, roll the appropriate number and type of hit dice for the servant and creature. The higher total is the stronger.
acceptedSevenLeaves.finding: The printed p.50–51 continuation supports the surprise result, detector d6 mapping, hit/grab process, Strength comparison, and appropriate number and type of hit dice fallback.

acceptedSevenLeaves.oldValue: Movement, attack frequency, damage, armor class and durability depend on shape, material and mass; the referee decides these values.
acceptedSevenLeaves.newValue: Movement depends on means of propulsion and weight. Examples: a large stone pedestal rocks forward 1″ per round, a stone statue moves 4″ per round, a wooden statue 8″ per round, and a light ivory stool 12″ per round; slithering is about 1″–2″ per round and rolling 3″–6″ per round.
acceptedSevenLeaves.finding: The page supports propulsion/weight dependence, the listed object movement examples, and slither/roll speeds.

acceptedSevenLeaves.oldValue: Flexible objects can obstruct, trip, bind or smother; harder objects can strike or crush.
acceptedSevenLeaves.newValue: Light, supple objects can only obscure vision, obstruct movement, bind, trip or smother. Light, hard objects can strike for 1–2 hit points or possibly obstruct and trip as light, supple objects; hard medium-weight objects can crush or strike for 2–8 hit points, and larger/heavier objects for 3–12, 4–16 or 5–20 hit points.
acceptedSevenLeaves.finding: The page supports the light/supple, light/hard, medium-weight, and larger/heavier damage/action branches.

exorciseComparatorClarityAddendum.oldValue: For each level of difference, subtract 1 percentage point when the cleric is lower; add 1 percentage point cumulatively when the cleric is higher. The source gives a 1%–100% base chance; the referee may set the base according to circumstances.
exorciseComparatorClarityAddendum.newValue: For each level of difference between the cleric and the possessor or possessing magic, subtract 1 percentage point when the cleric is lower; add 1 percentage point cumulatively when the cleric is higher. The source gives a 1%–100% base chance; the referee may set the base according to circumstances.
exorciseComparatorClarityAddendum.finding: Printed p.48 states the modifier compares the cleric’s experience level with the possessor’s level or the level of possessing magic; it then says the smaller number is the cleric’s level and the higher-level case adds +1% cumulatively. The new sentence makes that comparator explicit without changing the formula, adding a range unit, or resolving another rule. The exact current /conditions/2 value matches the proposed newValue.
exorciseComparatorClarityAddendum.gradeBoundary: Separate clarity-only confirmation. This leaf was ungraded in the existing mechanics ledger; keep it ungraded. No source-value verification status, target binding, or field-to-excerpt grade changes.
